proposition.claim:
A generic plane curve here is smooth and has dual singularities consisting only of ordinary nodes and cusps (pp. 1–2). For degree \(d=2k\), write \(p,n\) for the numbers of even and odd real ovals. The bitangent sign is unchanged if the two complementary sign regions are exchanged. Real bitangents with conjugate contact points contribute positively; for two real contacts the sign is the product of the two local side signs. These distinctions matter in passing from an unsigned count to \(t_s\).

For any field K of characteristic not2, a specified limiting chord defined over K deforms to a K-bitangent of Ct for t in K.

K=Q,k=2,C:w^2=product(u^2-a^2),a=1/2,2,1/3,3. Exact Newton triangle, smooth compactified two-section, eight distinct simple rational ramification values; no additional chord-concurrency condition is stated. Ct:(y^2-xz)^2-t^2*product(x-a^2*z)=0 is exactly the Proposition3.6 family. All Ct with0<t<3/25 are smooth over C; generic dual certified originally at t=1/1000 and hence outside finitely many parameters. Specified rational chords y=(2/5)(x+z) and y=(3/10)(x+z). The exact quadratic-square equivalence is used only for 0<|t|<3/25, where the V^4 coefficient is nonzero.

A generic plane curve here is smooth and has dual singularities consisting only of ordinary nodes and cusps (pp. 1–2). For degree \(d=2k\), write \(p,n\) for the numbers of even and odd real ovals. The bitangent sign is unchanged if the two complementary sign regions are exchanged. Real bitangents with conjugate contact points contribute positively; for two real contacts the sign is the product of the two local side signs. These distinctions matter in passing from an unsigned count to \(t_s\).

Real degree-k small perturbations R1,R2 with simple roots and floor(k/2) non-real roots.

k=2 or3 allowed in Lemma4.7. R1,R2 real polynomials with only simple roots.
